title: One-way functions in \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) from one-way functions
formal: Does the existence of a classical one-way function imply the existence of a classical one-way function computed by a polynomial-time uniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) circuit family?
definitions: The security parameter \(\lambda\) is supplied in unary. Algorithms are uniform probabilistic polynomial-time machines; security is against nonuniform polynomial-size classical circuit families. A function \(\nu (\lambda )\) is negligible if for every \(c>0, \nu (\lambda )\le \lambda ^{- c}\) for all sufficiently large \(\lambda\). Probabilities include setup, algorithm and adversary coins. No ideal oracle or additional trusted setup is supplied unless explicitly stated; arbitrary non-black-box implications are allowed. A one-way function is a deterministic polynomial-time map \(f:\{0,1\}*\to \{0,1\}\)* of polynomially bounded, length-dependent output size, such that every allowed inverter on \((1^{n},f(U_{n}))\) finds any n-bit preimage with negligible probability, for uniform \(U_{n}\). A polynomial-time uniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) family is generated from \(1^{n}\) in \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) time, has polynomial size and a universal constant depth, and uses fan-in-two \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}\) and unary NOT gates. Inversion security quantifies over all polynomial-size adversaries, not just shallow ones.

context_blocks.text: Local evaluation and global inversion difficulty are strikingly different requirements. An \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) one-way function has each output bit depend on only a constant number of input bits, while inverting the full output must defeat every polynomial-size adversary.

Known locality transformations start from stronger assumptions such as one-way functions in \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\). Those constructions establish plausible \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) cryptography, but they do not derive it from an arbitrary sequentially computable one-way function. The implication therefore asks whether cryptographic hardness can always be made local.

why: Identify whether extreme locality is inherent in minimal cryptographic hardness or requires a stronger assumption.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
